critiques.description: The mapping for req-RAG-001 marks the requirement as fully satisfied with high confidence based only on high-level architecture and operations notes about the ingestion pipeline. Those passages show that a single nightly pipeline is the only writer to the index and records source and timestamp, but they do not document the full success criteria of req-RAG-001 (e.g., specific governance, validation, provenance, or approval properties that might be required), so the claim of full satisfaction is not yet evidenced.
critiques.rationale: evd-002 and evd-023 document that the ingestion pipeline is the only writer to the retrieval index, runs nightly, reads from the help-center repository and resolved-tickets export, chunks and embeds content, and replaces changed chunks by source reference. This directly supports that writes are mediated through a single pipeline, but nothing in the provided evidence set describes the complete text or criteria of req-RAG-001 or shows that any additional governance elements it might require (such as validation steps, provenance guarantees, or change-approval controls) are implemented. Given that the mapping concludes req-RAG-001 is fully satisfied with high confidence, the current evidence base is insufficient to justify that conclusion; the assessment can at most state that some aspects of write governance are present, not that all requirement criteria are met.
